title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Shanghai Jiao Tong University-led team introduces EVA (Evolutionary Versatile Architect), a mixture-of-experts RNA foundation model with an 8,192-token context window trained on over 114 million full-length RNA sequences, covering tasks from mutational fitness prediction to de novo design of tRNAs, aptamers, CRISPR IscB omega-RNAs, mRNA and circular RNA therapeutics. Wet-lab assays show its best designed fluorescent aptamers roughly double both fluorescence intensity and binding affinity over the positive control, and it leads seven of nine benchmarks with over tenfold lower KL divergence to natural RNA secondary-structure distributions than the prior open-source RNA generator. The article body is paywalled; extractable content is the abstract, extended-data figure captions, data and code statements, funding and authorship.

insights.claim: EVA is a generative RNA foundation model combining a mixture-of-experts architecture with an 8,192-token context window, trained on over 114 million full-length RNA sequences spanning the breadth of evolutionary diversity.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Establishes the current scale reference point for RNA models, the modality lagging behind protein and DNA foundation models and closest to mRNA therapeutics revenue.
insights.quote: By integrating a mixture-of-experts architecture with an 8,192-token context window, EVA learns a unified, evolution-consistent representation of the RNA sequence space

insights.claim: Existing RNA generative models are described as lacking robust controllable design capability and constrained by short context windows that prevent modelling the evolutionary manifold of full-length transcripts.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Names context length and controllability, not raw parameter count, as the gating constraints in RNA design, which is where competing efforts will be judged.
insights.quote: existing RNA generative models lack robust controllable design capabilities and are constrained by short context windows

insights.claim: RNA sequence modelling appears to require a materially smaller learning rate than comparable DNA and protein mixture-of-experts models: the optimum found was 1e-4 versus 5e-4 for ProGen3 and 3e-4 for Evo2, implying distinct optimization dynamics for RNA.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Protein and genome model recipes do not transfer unchanged to RNA, which explains why RNA lagged and raises the cost of entry for teams assuming recipe reuse.
insights.quote: Our experiments demonstrate that the optimal learning rate for RNA is 1 × 10−4, suggesting distinct optimization dynamics for RNA sequence modeling.

insights.claim: Model scales explored during development spanned roughly 30 million to 1.4 billion parameters, with validation runs labelled 30M, 244M and 1400M plus a separate mid-training stage.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: RNA foundation models remain two to three orders of magnitude smaller than frontier language models, so capability gains are still cheap relative to compute budgets.
insights.locator: Source Data Extended Data Fig. 3 and Fig. 5 descriptions

insights.claim: Conditioning tokens are central to the design: RNA-type tokens during pre-training and taxonomic lineage conditioning introduced during mid-training, the latter reducing perplexity by disentangling species-specific constraints from universal RNA grammar.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Staged conditioning is the controllability mechanism that turns a generic sequence model into a steerable design tool — the transferable architectural idea here.
insights.quote: The introduction of lineage (taxonomic) conditioning in the mid-training stage further refines the RNA manifold by disentangling species-specific constraints from universal RNA grammar

themes.theme: Data curation as the real differentiator

insights.claim: RNA training data suffers more severe imbalance than protein data, with both numerous extremely large clusters and many small clusters, so direct training overfits abundant clusters; square-root cluster weighting achieved the best balance.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Sampling strategy, not architecture, decided whether training worked — the kind of unglamorous data-engineering edge that is hard for competitors to replicate from a paper.
insights.quote: Without sampling, direct training leads to overfitting on abundant clusters.

insights.claim: Evolutionary-conservation-based sampling deliberately down-samples highly conserved housekeeping RNAs such as rRNA and tRNA so the model spends capacity on the lower-conservation information-encoding and regulatory RNA classes.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Capacity is being steered toward the regulatory and coding RNAs that matter commercially for therapeutics, an explicit design choice rather than an emergent property.
insights.quote: Housekeeping RNAs are down-sampled, allowing the model to focus more on learning complex sequence patterns in information-encoding (info) and regulatory (reg) RNA classes.

insights.claim: RNA-type conditioning tokens are necessary because inter-RNA-type sequence similarity is low, meaning distinct RNA classes diverge substantially and cannot be learned efficiently as one undifferentiated corpus.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Explains why generic genomic language models underperform on RNA tasks: without class conditioning the training signal is diluted across incompatible sequence grammars.
insights.quote: highlighting the necessity of RNA-type conditioning tokens to enable efficient learning across diverse RNA families

insights.claim: Without RNA-type token conditioning, generation quality degrades measurably on three criteria: GC content outside the plausible 30-70% range, failure to emit a valid end-of-sequence token, and repetitive fragments exceeding 10% of the sequence.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete QC rubric for judging any generative nucleotide model, and names repetitive output as the characteristic failure mode of biological language models.
insights.quote: Repetitive generation is a common failure mode in biological language models.

insights.claim: The 114-million-sequence OpenRNA v1 training corpus, model checkpoints, tokenizers, benchmark files and source code are released openly on Hugging Face and GitHub under the Apache License 2.0.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Full open release of weights plus data removes the moat and accelerates diffusion of RNA design capability, including to competitors and to biosecurity-relevant actors.

insights.claim: The release goes unusually far on reproducibility, documenting file-level checksums, artifact provenance, versioned resource manifests, a recovered dense-control implementation and per-workflow validation records.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Signals rising reproducibility expectations in bio-AI publishing; provenance documentation is becoming a de facto requirement rather than a courtesy.

insights.claim: EVA-designed RNA aptamers improved both fluorescence intensity and binding affinity by roughly twofold over the positive control in wet-lab assays, with designs required to differ from the positive control by more than 60% at ligand-binding active sites.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Experimental, not in silico, improvement over an established benchmark aptamer is the rare validation that separates credible RNA design claims from predictor-on-predictor results.
insights.quote: In wet-lab assays, our best designed aptamers improve both fluorescence intensity and binding affinity by roughly twofold over the positive control.

insights.claim: EVA achieves state-of-the-art performance on seven of nine established benchmarks and generates sequences with more than tenfold lower Kullback-Leibler divergence to natural RNA secondary-structure feature distributions than the previous open-source RNA generator.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude distributional improvement, not a marginal benchmark win — the kind of jump that resets the baseline competitors must clear.
insights.quote: generating sequences with more than tenfold lower Kullback–Leibler divergence to natural RNA secondary-structure feature distributions than the previous open-source RNA generator

insights.claim: De novo generated tRNAs recovered natural folds as measured by TM-score against four matched controls (random, shuffled, profile-HMM and covariance-model) using both AlphaFold3 and Protenix, with only weak correlation between training-set sequence similarity and structural similarity.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The control design directly rebuts the memorization critique that dogs generative biology, and the dual-predictor check guards against single-tool artifacts.
insights.quote: weak correlation indicates fold recovery is not driven by interpolation from close training homologs

insights.claim: Fine-tuned EVA models generated 1,800 and 1,595 IscB omega-RNA guide variants respectively for two systems, with the explicit design goal of producing functional but more compact guides because IscB omega-RNAs are substantially larger than modern Cas guide RNAs.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Compact guides for compact editors is a direct delivery-payload constraint in gene therapy; generative shrinking of guide RNAs is a concrete commercial lever.
insights.quote: Because IscB ωRNAs are substantially larger than the guide RNAs of modern Cas systems, a key design goal is to generate functional yet more compact guides.

insights.claim: The model is applied to mRNA and circular RNA vaccine design including codon optimization, with results reported in minimum free energy and codon adaptation index per case and model.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Codon optimization and circRNA IRES design are where RNA generative models touch actual therapeutic manufacturing economics — stability and expression per dose.

insights.claim: One architecture handles the full task spectrum from zero-shot mutational fitness prediction across RNA, DNA and protein to context-aware sequence engineering, rather than requiring separate specialist models per RNA class.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Consolidation of a fragmented RNA tool landscape into one model mirrors what happened in protein ML, favouring platform owners over point-solution vendors.
insights.quote: EVA establishes a unified framework for a broad spectrum of RNA design tasks within a single architecture, ranging from mutational fitness prediction to context-aware sequence engineering.

themes.theme: Interpretability and steering borrowed from LLM research

insights.claim: Sparse autoencoders trained on EVA activations decompose dense representations into 8,192 sparse features that can be annotated against biological sequence elements and compared across taxonomic domains.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: LLM mechanistic-interpretability tooling is migrating wholesale into biology, which is the route to auditable and controllable biological design systems.

insights.claim: Feature sparsity in the RNA model reflects restricted token coverage rather than weak activation, with non-zero activation strength concentrated around a median of 0.5 for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic sequences.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Supports the view that learned features are genuinely selective biological detectors, strengthening the case that these models encode mechanism rather than correlation.
insights.quote: indicating that sparsity reflects restricted token coverage rather than reduced activation intensity

insights.claim: Lineage prefix prompts amplify the separation between eukaryotic and prokaryotic internal representations, raising the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic on feature-density distributions from 0.280 to 0.387 and increasing mean pairwise cosine distance between RNA-type expert-routing centroids by 40.5%.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Prompt-level conditioning measurably reorganizes internal routing, meaning control surfaces in bio-foundation models work much as prompting does in language models.

insights.claim: The top 2% most domain-differential sparse features, just 72 of 3,584, classify eukaryote versus prokaryote at logistic-regression AUC 0.702 plus or minus 0.062 versus a 0.501 shuffle baseline.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Statistically real but modest separability (AUC 0.70) is a useful reality check on how much interpretable structure these models currently expose.

insights.claim: Sparse-autoencoder feature steering shifted sequence likelihood toward target structural states in all 401 case-feature tests at some nonzero scale, with Wilcoxon p = 9.4e-68 and Cohen's d = 1.70, and RNAfold recovered diagnostic state-specific base pairs in generated sequences.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Steering latent features to flip RNA secondary structure would be a programmable control knob for riboswitches and sensors — early but strategically important.
insights.quote: 401/401 case-feature tests positive at some nonzero scale

insights.claim: The authors flag the steering result as preliminary and explicitly state the eight structural examples were hand-selected to illustrate recovery and are not a random sample for estimating success rates.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Unusually explicit self-limitation: the headline steering claim has no measured success rate, so do not extrapolate it to a usable design capability yet.
insights.quote: the eight structural examples were hand-selected to illustrate WT-like recovery and are not a random sample for estimating success rates

themes.theme: Provenance, funding and accessibility of the record

insights.claim: The work was produced by a 20-author, Shanghai-centred consortium led from Shanghai Jiao Tong University with Fudan, Tsinghua, Tongji, USTC and East China Normal collaborators, funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, Shanghai municipal science programmes and the CAST Young Elite Scientists Sponsorship Program.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
entities: National Natural Science Foundation of China
insights.so_what: Frontier open-weight RNA design capability is being produced and openly published by state-funded Chinese university consortia, a datapoint for biotech competitiveness and export-control debates.

insights.claim: Wet-lab validation was institutionally separated from model development, with in vitro transcription and fluorescence and binding-affinity measurement of designed aptamers performed and supervised by different authors than those who built the model.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Division of labour between modellers and experimentalists is what makes the twofold aptamer result more credible than typical in-silico-only design claims.

insights.claim: The published record for this paper is paywalled, with the extractable content limited to the abstract, extended-data and source-data captions, availability statements and authorship, while the full methods and results sit behind a USD 39.95 article purchase.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Analytical depth here is capped by access, though the model weights and training data are free — an inversion where the code is open and the paper is not.
insights.quote: This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution

insights.claim: A preprint version of the paper is available on bioRxiv, and the work was received in March 2026 and accepted in September 2026.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Roughly six-month review latency means the capability described has been publicly circulating since early 2026 — treat it as already diffused, not new.
insights.quote: A preprint version of the article is available at bioRxiv.
